subject: Post-call: multilingual evals & next steps (EU / APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lars Mueller <lars.mueller@globexbank.com>, Hana Suzuki <hana.suzuki@apac-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: multilingual evals & next steps (EU / APAC)

Hi Lars and Hana,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to hear more about the two pilots you described (transactional support in DE/FR and customer-facing chat in JP/KR). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard
- Globex Bank: high accuracy & auditability required for German/French channels; throughput target ~150 reqs/sec for peak hours.
- APAC Retail: low-latency chat in JP/KR with high coverage of colloquial Japanese/Korean and domain-specific product names.

Recommended initial model variants to evaluate
- redwood-13b-qa (fp16) — baseline for EU languages, strong few-shot QA precision
- redwood-13b-quant-8bit — cost-optimized variant to test latency/throughput trade-offs
- redwood-7b-multilingual — lighter-weight for APAC chat with tuned tokenization for JP/KR

Links / artifacts
- Prompt set (multilingual_prompt_set_v1.xlsx) — sample prompts per locale and intent (attached).
- Initial benchmark summary (PDF) — quick baseline numbers for latency and token cost.
- Shared folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-multilingual-evals

Proposed next steps (week of Apr 26)
1) You share the locale-specific test sets (de-fr JP-KR) or allow us to run on redacted samples.
2) We run a 1-week evaluation: 3 model variants, standard prompt sets + a stress test for peak throughput.
3) Joint sync at end of week to review quality regressions and perf/cost tradeoffs.

Questions for you
- For Globex Bank: are there any strict tokenization rules or legal redaction steps we need to include before ingest?
- For APAC Retail: do you have a priority list of intents (returns, order status, product info) we should weight higher in eval?

I'll loop in Neha (inference) and Vanessa (solutions) to own the evaluation orchestration and infra config.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: multilingual_prompt_set_v1.xlsx, initial_benchmark_summary.pdf

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Redaction: we can provide a redaction script that strips PII; we'll share the tool by EOD Monday. We also need SLA language around data retention for the pilot (30 days, audit logs required).
- Model concerns: security wants to ensure any quantized model still supports deterministic logging for auditability. Can Neha advise on how logging hooks are exposed for redwood-13b-quant-8bit?

We'll prep a sample de/fr test set (synthetic + anonymized real transcripts) and share via the shared drive. Confirming the timeline — a one-week run for the three variants on Apr 26 works.

Lars Mueller

Lars — quick reply on the quantized model logging question.

- redwood-13b-quant-8bit supports per-request tracing hooks that emit an immutable request id + token-level latency metrics. We can also emit masked prompt copies (PII redacted) into the audit log. Those controls are configurable at the route level for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted we provide a retention policy we can set to 30 days for pilot.
- For deterministic auditability (byte-level reproducibility) we recommend running the same model variant with a fixed seed and recording the KV cache warmup state; we can provide a runbook for Globex's audit team.

I'll provision an evaluation bucket and a sample inference config (batch size, max tokens, concurrency) for the Apr 26 run — will drop links in the folder.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
